correctness.rationale: On a finite labeled cycle the nested convex hulls are equal. A vertex of this hull can be an updated opinion only if all averaged opinions, including the updating label's old opinion, were at that vertex. Each vertex's occupancy set decreases by inclusion and is periodic, so is constant. With at most three labels, either all are fixed or just one can move inside a segment with one label fixed at each end. As its normalized coordinate increases it can only drop left-end trust and gain right-end trust. Its average increases with its own coordinate and weakly increases under both trust changes. Thus a strict displacement cannot return, even at a discontinuity. I independently recomputed the witness using squared distances and the integer ray equation 5|dy|=-dx for dx<0: the moving neighborhoods are {x,c} and {x,a,b,c}, all three anchors trust only themselves in both states, and the nonidentical configurations return in two steps.
residual_risks: Sharpness is attained in dimension two and embeds in higher dimensions, not asserted in dimension one by the exhibited orbit; the exclusion is dimension independent.

Homogeneity is a hypothesis of the frozen theorem, not a proved necessary condition: the argument for the lower bound also works for static agent-specific star-shaped confidence sets, because only the possible moving label's set is used. The prose claim that homogeneity is essential should not be read as a mathematical conclusion.
This is an exclusion of finite periods, not a convergence theorem.

value.rationale: The lower bound resolves whether the published four-agent construction needs four ordinary agents at all. The persistent extreme-label argument is structural and works despite discontinuous radial boundaries and arbitrary ambient dimension; it is not only a check of special parameter examples or two-cycles. The result supplies an exact population threshold in the stated setting.
residual_risks: The constructive half is prior and is not counted as a contribution; the threshold does not characterize more general recurrence.
